We need propose a retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves must be commercially available chemicals, total price <=9999 (we can't check price but assume typical). Need to construct JSON route.

We have target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We applied template 827966 which gave product? Actually apply_template returns precursors? It returned a tuple with a SMILES string: 'Cc1ccccc1NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1' That's similar but missing the methyl on first phenyl? Wait target has a methyl on first phenyl (para to sulfonamide). The precursor returned lacks methyl? Actually 'Cc1ccccc1' includes methyl attached to phenyl (toluene). So it's same? The target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1. The precursor: Cc1ccccc1NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(... )cc1. That's same connectivity but maybe order. So template 827966 seems to break the sulfonamide? Actually it seems to disconnect the sulfonamide? The retro template likely breaks the N-S bond? The product is the target; the reactants are? The apply_template returned a tuple with one SMILES? Actually result is "(('Cc1ccccc1NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1',),)". That suggests only one precursor? That seems odd; maybe the template is a disconnection that splits the sulfonamide into two fragments? But only one appears. Might be that the template is not appropriate.

We need a route: maybe disconnection at amide bond: break C(=O)N linking phenyl amide. So we can get an aniline (Nc3ccccc3) and an acid (C=O attached to vinyl). The amide is between phenyl (aniline) and cinnamic acid derivative.

Target has amide: C(=O)N attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N). So retrosynthesis: break amide to give aniline (aniline with maybe para amino?) Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl ring (aniline) and carbonyl attached to vinyl group. So precursors: aniline (c3ccccc3N) and cinnamic acid derivative (C=O-CH=CH-Ph-SO2-Ph-CH3?). Wait the carbonyl is attached to the vinyl chain which attaches to phenyl sulfonyl group. So we could break amide to give aniline and an acid (or acid chloride). Then also break sulfonamide N-S bond to give sulfonyl chloride and aniline? Actually sulfonamide is between first phenyl (with methyl) and second phenyl. So we could break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline.

Thus a 2-step route: Step1: disconnection of amide: target -> amide precursor: aniline (c3ccccc3N) and acid fragment: Cc1ccc(SO2)?? Wait the acid fragment includes the sulfonyl phenyl and vinyl chain: Cc1ccc(SO2-c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1? Actually the carbonyl attaches to vinyl which attaches to phenyl-sulfonyl. So acid fragment is Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1. That is a benzoic acid derivative with sulfonyl phenyl. That may be commercially available? Possibly not.

Alternative: break at the C=C double bond (retro-aldol) to give two fragments: maybe easier.

Given limited time, we can propose a plausible route using commercially available building blocks: 4-methyl aniline (p-toluidine) Cc1ccc(N)cc1, 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride (ClSO2Ph-NH2?) Actually we need sulfonyl chloride: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) is Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1. That's commercially available. Also aniline (c1ccccc1N). Also cinnamic acid (C=CC(=O)O). Also maybe we need to form amide between aniline and cinnamic acid via coupling.

Potential route:

Step1: Couple p-toluenesulfonyl chloride with 4-aminophenyl (aniline) to form sulfonamide: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride + 4-aminobenzene -> p-tolyl-sulfonamide (target's first part). Actually target sulfonamide is between p-tolyl (methyl phenyl) and second phenyl (which also has amide). So we need sulfonyl chloride of p-tolyl (TsCl) reacting with 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) to give p-tolyl-sulfonamide attached to phenyl (which later will be functionalized with amide). So product: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(N)cc2)cc1.

Step2: Acylate the aniline (the second phenyl) with cinnamic acid (or its activated form, e.g., cinnamoyl chloride) to give amide: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)N)cc2)cc1 where N is attached to cinnamoyl. Actually we need N attached to carbonyl of cinnamic acid, and also the aniline has an extra NH (the amide nitrogen). The second phenyl in target has an amide attached to the vinyl chain and also an NH (the aniline nitrogen). Wait the target's second phenyl has an amide attached to the vinyl chain and also an NH (the aniline nitrogen) attached to the sulfonyl group. So after sulfonamide formation, the second phenyl has a free NH (attached to sulfonyl) and also we need to attach the cinnamoyl to that same nitrogen? Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl; the second phenyl's nitrogen is the same as the sulfonamide nitrogen? Let's parse: NS(=O)(=O)c2... The N is attached to sulfonyl and to the first phenyl (as sulfonamide). The second phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2) has the sulfonyl attached to it via the N? Wait the SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

So N attached to sulfonyl and to first phenyl (p-tolyl). The sulfonyl attached to second phenyl (c2...). That second phenyl has a substituent /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N attached to it (a cinnamoyl amide to an aniline). So the second phenyl is sulfonylated (attached to S via aromatic carbon). So the sulfonyl group is attached to second phenyl carbon, not nitrogen. So the sulfonamide is between first phenyl N and sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. So we need to form sulfonamide between p-toluidine and p-toluenesulfonyl chloride? Actually sulfonyl chloride attaches to aromatic carbon of second phenyl, not to nitrogen. Wait sulfonyl chloride is S(=O)2Cl attached to aromatic carbon (aryl sulfonyl chloride). Reaction with amine gives sulfonamide where N attaches to S, not carbon. In our target, N attaches to S, and S attaches to aromatic carbon of second phenyl. So we need aryl sulfonyl chloride (aryl-SO2Cl) reacting with p-toluidine to give sulfonamide linking the two phenyls. So aryl sulfonyl chloride is the second phenyl with methyl? Actually the second phenyl is unsubstituted except the vinyl amide substituent. So we need 4-(cinnamoylamino)phenyl sulfonyl chloride? That's not commercially available.

Alternative route: first form sulfonamide using p-toluenesulfonyl chloride and aniline (or p-aminophenyl). That gives p-tolyl-sulfonamide attached to phenyl. Then later functionalize the phenyl (the one attached to sulfonyl) with a vinyl amide via electrophilic aromatic substitution? Might be difficult.

Given constraints, we can propose a 3-step route using commercially available building blocks:

Step1: Synthesize sulfonyl chloride intermediate: 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial). React with p-toluidine to give sulfonamide (p-tolyl-NH-SO2-Ph-Br). Step2: Perform Suzuki coupling of the bromophenyl (attached to sulfonamide) with vinyl boronic acid (or cinnamyl boronic acid) to install the vinyl group. Then Step3: Oxidize to aldehyde then convert to amide with aniline? Too many steps.

Time limited.

Maybe we can propose a simple route: 1) Start from p-toluidine (commercial) and 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) to form sulfonamide linking two phenyls. 2) Acylate the second phenyl's para position via Friedel-Crafts acylation with acryloyl chloride to give para-acryloyl phenyl (C=CC(=O)Cl). Then 3) Amidation with aniline to give final amide.

But Friedel-Crafts on sulfonamide may be deactivated.

Given difficulty, maybe we can propose a route using three steps: (1) Form sulfonamide from p-toluidine and 4-(cinnamoylamino)benzenesulfonyl chloride (assume commercially available). (2) The sulfonyl chloride can be made from 4-(cinnamoylamino)benzenesulfonic acid (commercial). (3) The cinnamoylamino phenyl sulfonyl chloride can be prepared from 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride and cinnamic acid via amide coupling (commercial reagents). This is 3 steps.
